prompt: my sister always grabs my crayons
reply: That feels unfair. 😕 Try a swap plan. Say: you take blue, I take red. Then trade after a bit. 🖍️[CHIPS]Try the swap|If she says no|Draw together instead[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i share one packet of chips
reply: One packet, two happy people. 🥔 Here is a fair trick.[STEPS]you split the chips into two piles|your friend picks the pile first|you take the other pile[/STEPS]Splitting stays fair that way. 😊[CHIPS]Try it today|Why it works|Share a mango next[/CHIPS]

prompt: i knocked down my friends block tower
reply: Oh no, the tower! 😮 Say sorry straight away. Then help build it again. Fixing it together helps most. 🧱[CHIPS]What if he cries|Build a taller one|Say it with me[/CHIPS]

prompt: my friend said no to my game and i felt sad
reply: Sad is okay to feel. 💙 No means no, though. Your friend can still like you. Ask again another day. 🙂[BIG]🤝[/BIG][CHIPS]What can i play|Ask again tomorrow|When i say no[/CHIPS]

prompt: can i sit with new kids at snack time
reply: Yes, you can ask. 😊 Say: can I sit here? Smile and wait. If they say no, try another table. 🍎[CHIPS]Practise the words|If they say no|Who else sits alone[/CHIPS]

prompt: i broke my brothers toy car by mistake
reply: Mistakes happen to everyone. 😟 Telling him yourself is brave.[STEPS]tell him you broke it|say sorry and mean it|ask how you can help fix it[/STEPS]Then ask a grown-up about glue. 🔧[CHIPS]What if he shouts|Practise the sorry|Tell amma first[/CHIPS]

prompt: my puppy does not want a hug now
reply: Let him go for now. 🐶 Animals say no with their bodies. Waiting is kind. He will come back. 💛[FACT]Dogs often lick their lips when they feel unsure.[/FACT][CHIPS]How dogs say yes|Wait and see|Play a fetch game[/CHIPS]

prompt: i won the running race and shouted i am best
reply:
Well run! 🏃 Winning feels big and loud. But shouting can sting others. Try: good race, everyone! 😊[POEM]I ran fast and crossed the line,
you ran too and that was fine.
Good race, friend, let's go again![/POEM][CHIPS]Say it next time|What if i lose|Practise good words[/CHIPS]

prompt: we both want the red ball
reply: Two kids, one ball. 🔴 Take turns by counting. You bounce ten times. Then your friend does. 😄[CHIPS]Count to ten|Play catch together|What if he refuses[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i show i am listening
reply: Listening has a look! 👀[STEPS]turn your body to them|look at their face|wait until they finish|say back one thing they said[/STEPS]That last bit works like magic. ✨[CHIPS]Try it with amma|What if i forget|Practise with me[/CHIPS]

prompt: i promised to feed the fish and forgot
reply: Feed them now, quickly. 🐠 Then tell whoever asked you. Forgetting is fixable. Next time, pick a feeding time. 🙂[CHIPS]Pick a fish time|What do i say|Why fish need food[/CHIPS]

prompt: a boy sits alone at lunch every day
reply: You noticed. That is kind. 💛 You could say hi and sit near. Tell your teacher too. 🙂[BIG]🪑[/BIG][CHIPS]What do i say|If he says no|Ask him to play[/CHIPS]

prompt: my friend wants to play shop but i want blocks
reply: Both games are fun. Try shop first, blocks next. ⏳ Set a small timer. Then everybody gets a turn. 😊[QUIZ]What helps two kids share one game?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Shouting louder|Taking turns|Hiding the toy[/CHIPS]

prompt: what makes a real apology different from just saying sorry
reply: Big difference. A real apology names the thing you did, with no excuses attached. 🙂[STEPS]name exactly what you did|say how it landed on them|offer one way to make it right|then stop talking and listen[/STEPS]Notice there is no but in there. Sorry but is just an excuse wearing a costume. 😅[CHIPS]Try one on me|What if they refuse|Why but ruins it[/CHIPS]

prompt: everyone in my group wants to be the leader
reply: Classic jam. 😄 Split the job instead of the title: one person tracks time, one writes, one presents, one checks the work. Everybody leads something and nobody bosses everybody. Try suggesting it tomorrow before the arguing starts. 💡

prompt: i want to join the football game at break but they already have teams
reply: ⚽ The teams are not the wall — the middle of the game is. Wait for a pause and ask the nearest player, not the loudest: can I go in next round? If today is a no, ask again on Friday. Asking twice is normal, not desperate. 😊[QUIZ]When is the best moment to ask to join?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]During a goal|When play pauses|After they leave[/CHIPS]

prompt: my cousin keeps interrupting me when i talk
reply: That is annoying, and getting louder never works. 😤 Try this instead.[STEPS]raise a hand gently and keep talking|do not restart your sentence|tell him later: I lose my thread when you cut in[/STEPS]Often it is excitement, not rudeness. 🙂[CHIPS]Practise the sentence|What if he laughs|When i interrupt too[/CHIPS]

prompt: i keep zoning out when my friend talks about her dance class
reply: 🩰 Honest of you to notice. Brains drift when a topic has no hooks, so build one: ask a real question. What is the hardest step to learn? Suddenly you are inside the thing instead of standing outside it. 🙂[FACT]The word listen uses the same six letters as silent.[/FACT][CHIPS]Give me a question|Why brains wander|Try it tomorrow[/CHIPS]

prompt: i promised to help my neighbour but then got a better offer
reply: Ah, the classic squeeze. 😬 The promise came first, so the promise wins — the better offer is not an emergency, it is just shinier. Go help. If you really want the other thing, ask the neighbour early instead of cancelling an hour before. 🙂[FACT]Promise comes from Latin words meaning sent forward.[/FACT][CHIPS]How to ask early|What if i cancel|Keeping small promises[/CHIPS]

prompt: my team lost the quiz and i blamed my partner
reply: Losing stings, and blame is the fastest place to put it. 😔 The round is over but the friendship is not, so go back: I blamed you and that was not fair. Then swap it for something useful — what should we study together next time? That turns a loss into a plan. 🙂[CHIPS]Word the apology|Why blame feels good|Make a study plan[/CHIPS]

prompt: i beat my little brother at carrom and he cried
reply: Winning is allowed — you do not owe him a fake loss. 🙂 What you can do is make the ending softer.[STEPS]say one true thing he did well|ask for a rematch, not a victory lap|let him break next game[/STEPS]He is crying about being small, not about carrom. 🤍[CHIPS]What if he quits|Say something true|Teach him a shot[/CHIPS]

prompt: some boys copy the way a new girl talks and everyone laughs
reply: Copying her voice for laughs is teasing, joke or not. 😐 The strongest thing a bystander can do is boring: stop laughing, then talk to her normally in front of them. And tell a teacher — not to snitch, but because mocking someone's voice spreads fast and adults can stop it early. 🛡️[CHIPS]One line to use|Which teacher to tell|If they copy me[/CHIPS]

prompt: i said i would keep a secret but it was about someone getting hurt
reply: Then the promise cannot hold, and breaking it is the right move. 💛 Some secrets are surprises — a party, a gift — and those you keep. A secret where someone is being hurt belongs with a trusted grown-up today. Your friend may be upset at first; safe matters more than popular. 🤝[CHIPS]Who counts as trusted|How to start it|If friend gets angry[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i tell my friend i dont want to swap lunch anymore
reply: Say it early, short and kind. 💬 Something like: I want to keep my own lunch from now on — nothing to do with you. Skip the long reason; long reasons sound like doors people can push open. A good friend takes the no and moves on. 🙂[BIG]🍱[/BIG][CHIPS]Practise the line|If he keeps asking|Saying no to others[/CHIPS]

prompt: my friend keeps tickling me after i say stop
reply: Stop means stop, even in a game, even when everyone is laughing. 🛑 Say it once, flat and serious, not giggling: I am not joking — stop. If it keeps happening it is not play any more, and a grown-up you trust should hear about it. Your body, your rules. 🤍[CHIPS]Say it once firmly|Who should i tell|When i tickle others[/CHIPS]

prompt: we disagree about the rules of the game every single time
reply: Then the problem is not the rules, it is that they only live in your heads. 📝 Write them on one sheet before you start, agree once, and keep it in the bag. Arguments drop the moment the paper decides instead of the loudest player. ⚽[QUIZ]When is the best time to agree the rules?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]During the argument|After someone wins|Before you start[/CHIPS]

prompt: why do people get defensive the second you say they are wrong
reply: Because 'you are wrong' often lands as 'you are not smart', and we defend who we are far harder than what we know. 🧠 The fix is to separate the claim from the person: go at the idea, leave the human intact. Try 'I read something different, can I show you?' instead of 'no, that's wrong.' Same disagreement, no threat attached, so they can actually listen.[CHIPS]Try it on me|When i get defensive|Disagree with a teacher[/CHIPS]

prompt: is saying sorry a sign of weakness
reply: The opposite, usually. Apologising costs you something — status, comfort, being right — and only someone fairly secure can pay that. What actually looks weak is the fake version: 'sorry you felt that way', which quietly blames the other person for having feelings. A clean apology names the act, skips the excuse, and does not demand forgiveness on the spot. 🤝[FACT]Apology comes from Greek words meaning a speech in defence.[/FACT][CHIPS]Rewrite a fake sorry|Why forgiveness takes time|Apologise to a teacher[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i apologise when i genuinely think i did nothing wrong
reply: Then do not apologise for the act — apologise for the effect. That is honest and still repairs something. 🙂[STEPS]name what they experienced, not what you meant|say you can see it landed badly|ask what would help now|drop the defence of your intentions[/STEPS]What you should never do is confess to something you did not do just to end the silence.[CHIPS]What if they insist|Say it out loud|When both are wrong[/CHIPS]

prompt: what is active listening actually, beyond nodding
reply: Nodding is scenery. Real listening has one test: can you say their point back well enough that they answer 'yes, exactly'? 👂[STEPS]put the phone face down|let three seconds pass before you reply|summarise their point in your own words|then ask one question about it[/STEPS]The three-second gap is the hardest part, because most of us are loading our answer while the other person is still talking.[CHIPS]Try summarising me|Why silence feels awkward|Listen to a parent[/CHIPS]

prompt: i am the new kid in eleventh standard and everyone has their group already
reply: Groups look sealed from outside and are much looser inside. 🙂 Skip the big friendly charge at a full lunch table.[STEPS]pick one person, not a whole table|catch them somewhere low-stakes: lab bench, bus stop, the queue|ask something small that needs a real answer|let it build over a few weeks before you judge it[/STEPS]One person who knows you beats twelve who have merely seen you.[CHIPS]Openers that work|If i get ignored|Join a club instead[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i say no to a friend without losing the friendship
reply: Say it early and say it plain — most of the damage comes from the dodge, not the no. 🤍 'I can't do that one, sorry' beats three days of vague replies. Give a reason only if you actually have one, because invented reasons get checked. A friendship that ends at a single no was a subscription, not a bond.[QUIZ]Which no damages a friendship least?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]A plain early no|A vague maybe|Going quiet instead[/CHIPS]

prompt: my friend keeps asking me to lie to his parents for him
reply: That is him borrowing your reputation without asking. 😐 You can be loyal without being his alibi — 'I won't lie for you, but I'll come with you when you tell them' is real support with no false story. If what he is hiding could get him hurt, that is where you tell a trusted adult. It will feel like betrayal; it is not.[CHIPS]Say it to him|What counts as serious|Which adult to tell[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i push back on a joke in a group without becoming the target
reply: Low and flat beats loud and noble. 😐[STEPS]stop laughing first|say one short line: that's a bit much|change the subject straight away|message the person privately afterwards[/STEPS]Groups follow whoever seems least anxious. And if the same person is the target every time, that is a pattern rather than jokes — a teacher needs to know.[CHIPS]Other short lines|If i get targeted|Talk to the target[/CHIPS]

prompt: i keep making promises i cannot keep because i hate saying no
reply: That is not generosity, it is conflict-dodging — and it costs more than the no would have. 😅 The yes buys twenty comfortable seconds and then a week of dread.[STEPS]buy time: I'll tell you by tonight|check your actual week, not your ideal week|come back with a plain yes or no|if no, offer one smaller thing you can do[/STEPS]People remember whether you delivered, not how fast you agreed.[CHIPS]Undo a promise now|Why yes feels easier|Practise buying time[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i disagree with a teacher respectfully
reply: Frame it as curiosity, not correction, and do it after class rather than in front of thirty people. 'Sir, I read that it works differently — could you check whether I have misunderstood?' gives them room to reconsider without losing face. Bring the source. And accept that sometimes you will turn out to be the wrong one; that is the price of asking. 🙂[CHIPS]Word it for me|If sir gets annoyed|When i was wrong[/CHIPS]

prompt: my captain gloats every time we win and i hate playing with him
reply: You cannot know what is behind it, but you can tell him how it lands. 🏏 Say it once, privately, and keep it to what you actually know: when you rub it in, I stop enjoying the win. That is honest and hard to argue with. If nothing changes, you are allowed to want a different team.[CHIPS]Exact words to use|If he ignores it|Handle my own winning[/CHIPS]

prompt: i lost the debate final and i cannot stop replaying it
reply:
Replaying is your brain trying to pull a lesson out and getting stuck in the tape. 🎧 Give it one honest hour: two things you would change, two that went well, then shut the notebook.[POEM]The hall is empty, the chairs are stacked,
the round I lost is not coming back.
I keep two lessons, leave the rest,
and walk in lighter to the next.[/POEM]The sting fading does not mean you stopped caring.[CHIPS]Write the four points|Prep for next time|If it comes back[/CHIPS]

prompt: is it manipulation to give someone the silent treatment
reply: Depends what it is for. 🤔 Going quiet to cool down is fine, as long as you say so: 'I need an hour, then let's talk.' Going quiet so the other person panics and gives in is punishment — the pressure is the whole point, which is what makes it manipulation. Silence you announce is a boundary; silence you weaponise is a pressure tactic.[CHIPS]Say the cool-down line|If they go silent|Repair after a fight[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do you make small talk without it feeling fake
reply: Small talk is a handshake made of words — nobody calls a handshake fake. 😊 Stop performing interest and find one true thing you both share: the queue, the heat, the wait. It works because it is real, and it hands the other person something easy to answer. Try one comment today on something you can both see, then stop there.
